newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 1-yr bond price seen down, demand small.
newsitem.headline: Polish 1-yr bond price seen down, demand small.

text.p: The minimum price of Poland's one-year index-linked bonds at today's 200 million zloty tender is likely to fall on small demand as investors turn to the more liquid and attractively priced 52-week T-bills, dealers said.
The one-year bond is indexed to the year-on-year consumer price index from two months before maturity in June 4, 1998.

"The one-year bond is not liquid compared with the 52-week T-bill so its price should reflect not only the expected fall in inflation but also a bonus for the fact that it is not liquid," said Andrzej Jasinski, bond dealer at Pekao SA.
Inflation is widely expected to drop to 13 percent in December 1997, and, consequently to be even lower in April 1998, which would be the month used for yield calculations.
Dealers said the price of the bonds should therefore be no higher than 90.00-91.00 to make its yield match the 21.68 percent average yield of the 52-week T-bill from the last tender.

"Also, with falling inflation it is better to invest in fixed interest instruments than in floaters, so I would be surprised if demand at the tender amounted to even half the offer," said Grzegorz Raupuk, bond dealer at Bank Gdanski SA
At the last tender in February the minimum price of the paper was 94.48 and the average price 94.62 with demand topping the 348 million zloty offer but only 89 million-zlotys worth of paper sold.
